clinician.final_diagnosis: Type II hereditary antithrombin deficiency (ATD) due to SERPINC1 mutation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old male presented with a 4-year history of recurrent bilateral paroxysmal headaches (afternoon onset, 1-2 hours duration, relieved by rest) and occasional limb numbness when emotional, with negative neurological examination. Brain MRI revealed multiple discrete hyperintense lesions in periventricular deep white matter and frontal/parietal lobes bilaterally, distributed perpendicular to the lateral ventricles without enhancement. Whole exon sequencing identified a novel heterozygous missense mutation in the SERPINC1 gene (1q25.1), with Sanger sequencing confirming the mutation in the father. Laboratory studies demonstrated decreased AT III activity (72.2%, reference 80-120%) with normal AT III antigen levels (235 mg/L, reference 180-392 mg/L), consistent with type II ATD. The father exhibited a similar biochemical profile (AT III activity 75.1%, antigen 263.3 mg/L) with asymptomatic white matter lesions on MRI. Additional workup revealed a patent foramen ovale via transcranial Doppler and transthoracic echocardiography. The patient underwent percutaneous PFO closure and received oral antiplatelet therapy, with follow-up at 1 and 6 months showing significant improvement in headache pain degree, attack frequency, and duration despite unchanged MRI lesions.
